Level 4 Test Purpose
This script relates to level 4 functional performance testing of 33kV Ring Main Unit (DC) for ECX project charter. Developed in line with the global/technical specifications and basis of design.
Prerequisites:
Confirm there are no critical issues open for equipment impacting Level 4.
Level 2 and Level 3 commissioning equipment start-up checklists are complete
Level 3 controls Point-to-Point (P2P) and alarm verification checklists for equipment are completed.
Confirm all applicable equipment Sequence of Operation [SoO] are created, approved, and reviewed for testing.
Equipment pre-test meeting is held with all parties to review the testing procedures, requirements and any constraints. All participants and affected personnel are notified prior to testing.
These functional test procedures reviewed and approved by the commissioning team.
Safeties and operating ranges reviewed and approved by Owner’s Representative.
BMS/EPMS network is operational - end to end.

All control system functions for this and all interlocking systems are programmed and operable per contract documents, including final set points and schedules with debugging, loop tuning and sensor calibrations completed. All point-to-point (P2P) verification has been completed, documented, reviewed and accepted.
BMS Controls: interlocks, graphics, automatic sequencing, and other controlling functions are complete.
Requested Staffing
The following staff members are available on-site to operate their equipment, assist and oversee completion of approved test procedure
Mechanical Contractor
Electrical Contractor
BMS Vendor
33kV Switchgear (DC) Vendor
Energy Marshall
33kV Chargeman DC Building
33kV Chargeman CLS
Transformer Vendor (as required)

Level 4 Equipment Pre-Checks

Record initial test conditions specific to unit being tested at component level. Conditions recorded should be observed at unit locally and through BMS graphical interface. Test section verifies components are operating and within range, as well as verifies components are represented correctly at the BMS level.
RECORD SCREENSHOT of Graphic GUI initial screenshot prior to start testing
Review Screenshot data and confirm value inputs are reliable and easily readable at BMS front end.
Unit Identification and description is correct on the graphic display
All graphic animations of equipment actions have been programmed and are complete
All BMS points are correctly and neatly represented on the graphic display (space temperature, filter status, temp setpoint etc.)
Review & Verify the Graphics are correct and represent all devices fitted in the field
Review & Verify the Graphics are as per Status A Approved Graphics
Verify & record the firmware version
Pre-Record Initial setpoints per SOO/DOO, Specification, or Equipment Submittal to confirm system has been configured to control to the correct parameters.
Note - SOO requirements supercede conflicting parameters.
Record & Confirm the following:-
Cooling Control Parameter
Conduct the following preliminary checks prior to functional performance testing:
Confirm the neutral to ground bonding is complete per project documentation.
Confirm there are no outstanding integration works.
Confirm power meters have been configured.
Confirm the 33kV Consumer Substation is ready for operation, with no alarms present.
Confirm the control power is operational, in automatic operation and free of alarms, ready for functional performance testing.
Confirm Lock Out Tag Out (LOTO) has been implemented at the designated RMU's incoming breaker.
Equipment Physical Inspection and Preliminary Checks
Inspect equipment installation for compliance with approved submittal, construction details, and industry standards.
Confirm installation is inspected for compliance with approved submittal, construction details, and industry standards.
Confirm a complete L2/3 verification of this item of equipment has been conducted prior to L4 test commencing
Conduct a pre physical inspection of equipment prior to L4 test commencing
De-energization and LOTO
Authorized person to de-energize and isolate supplies at upstream disconnection points as per isolation and LOTO procedure
LOTO to be applied by authorized person
LOTO to be applied by BVPI personnel
Functional Performance Test Procedure
A. Visual Inspection
Visual Inspections - Ground system
Proper earthing of MV cable shielding (If applicable)
Proper earthing of the Switchgear to the Enclosure Earth point
Proper earthing of Building Earthing System to Enclosure Earth point
All Earth cables properly torqued (torque marks visible)
Proper Earthing to the TX Earthing terminal
Proper Earthing of building ground array to TX Earthing terminal
Transformer star point installed correctly on secondary side of transformer
Visual Inspections- 33kV RMU Switchgear
Switchboard Exterior
Asset tag is attached
Hazard warning labels fitted
Equipment Rating plate matches technical submittal
Painted surfaces are not scratched
All components properly labelled.
Proper craftsmanship and installation methods used
High Voltage safety matting is installed
All mechanical disconnects labelled correctly
Operating Handel is available and installed at location as per OEM manual
Auxiliary circuits labelled/identified
Room heating and ventilation is operational with temperature thermostat set points are all correct
Confirm Gas pressure is Normal
Switchboard Interior
Adequate cleanliness of the switchgear
No damage to visible power and/or earth cables
B. Supply Verification of 33kV RMU Switchgear
Power Supply Verification
Ensure both control power supplies are available and energized/temporary power supply is allowed
Turn OFF auxiliary power supply
Ensure all auxiliary equipment (relays etc.) remains energized, On Battery Supply
Record External Aux Control Supply current and Voltage
Protection relay is mapped as per relay mapping documentation
Protection relay settings as per protection study documentation
Cubicle Condensation Heaters
Record humidity setpoint
Simulate the humidity setpoint
Verify the heater function
Reset thermostat to pre test setpoint
Repeat the above steps for each cubicle heaters
C. BMS Monitoring and Protection Verification
Verify all points by actuating the device or simulate the condition as close to the device as safely possible.
A 10% inspection will be conducted and once cxa confirms and dependent on the success of these the CxA may check 100%
Screenshots to be taken and attached/uploaded to folder at end of test

D. Operation - 33kV RMU Breaker Operation, Monitoring Interlock Validation
NOTE: Qualified personnel to operate equipment only - If operation of equipment can be conducted remotely, this is preferred to ensure all safety precautions are taken.
G.1 Breaker Function
Local Operation - Incomer 1
Breaker Function
Using handle, verify operation for local OPEN/CLOSED LBS on BMS
Local display
BMS equipment page
Using handle, verify operation of OPEN/CLOSED  Earth Switch for interlock between LBS and ES
Verify castell key interlock between LBS and ES
Local display
BMS equipment page
Acknowledge all alarms
Reset manually
Local Operation - Incomer 2
Breaker Function
Using handle, verify operation for local OPEN/CLOSED LBS on BMS
Local display
BMS equipment page
Using handle, verify operation of OPEN/CLOSED  Earth Switch for interlock between LBS and ES
Verify castell key interlock between LBS and ES
Local display
BMS equipment page
Acknowledge all alarms
Reset manually
Local Operation - Outgoing Feeder
Breaker Function
Select selector switch LOCAL/REMOTE to LOCAL
Using Rotary Switch, verify operation for local OPEN/CLOSED CB on BMS
Using Breaker Mounted Push Button, verify operation for local OPEN/CLOSED CB on BMS
Using Controller, verify operation for local OPEN/CLOSED CB on BMS
Using Handle, verify operation for Local Disconnector Switch OPEN/CLOSED on BMS
Using Handle, verify operation for local OPEN/CLOSED CB on BMS
Using Handle, verify operation for Earth Switch OPEN/CLOSED on BMS
Using pendant switch, verify OPEN/CLOSE CB operation.
Breaker Motorized Spring Charger Fault/Loss of Supply
Ensure CB in close position
Turn OFF MCB of motorized spring charger
Verify Circuit Breaker will not shunt trip
Using Push Button OPEN Circuit Breaker
Circuit Breaker opens
CLOSE circuit breaker
Circuit Breaker will not close
Turn ON MCB of motorized spring charger
Spring gets charged
Using Push Button CLOSE Circuit Breaker
Circuit Breaker closes
Acknowledge all alarms
Reset manually
End of Test
Confirm all simulated variables are restored to project requirement
Confirm that all equipment panels and covers are in place and secured.

Level 4  Functional Performance Test Procedure - MSB w/ ATS
A. Monitoring - Breaker  and ATS Operation, Indication and Monitoring Validation
NOTE: Qualified personnel to operate equipment only - If operation of equipment can be conducted remotely, this is preferred to ensure all safety precautions are taken.
Conduct / simulate the following alarms, validating to the local HMI and BMS network:
Manually close each circuit breaker and validate status to BMS network
Confirm all circuit breakers reflect accurately on BMS network and local HMI.
For outgoing circuits, Confirm the digital power meter voltage reference is connected to the output of each circuit breaker - DPM displays 0 volts with circuit breaker open.

For incoming circuits, isolate the upstream supply with the local breaker closed to confirm the digital power meter voltage reference is connected to the lineside of each circuit breaker - DPM displays 0 volts with upstream supply isolated.
Reinstate all circuit breakers to there nominal state.
Confirm no alarms are present on BMS network and local HMI.
Generate a surge arrestor fault alarm by removing one of the phase supply fuses.
Confirm surge arrestor fault alarm on BMS network and local HMI.
Reinstate the supply fuse.
Confirm surge arrestor fault alarm on BMS network and local HMI is no longer active.
Generate a loss of communications alarm by removing the BMS lan cable to the network switch.
Confirm Loss of Communications alarm on BMS network and local HMI.
Reinstate the network cable.
Confirm the alarm on BMS network and local HMI is no longer active.
B. Operation - Electrical Interlock Validation
NOTE: Qualified personnel to operate equipment only - If operation of equipment can be conducted remotely, this is preferred to ensure all safety precautions are taken.
At the upstream generator and utility, place the generator into manual or off mode and open the local generator circuit breaker.
Place the ATS controller into manual via the selector switch.
Confirm generator and utility supply isolated from outgoing switchboard.
Installed LOTO to RMU Outgoing Breaker and Generator Circuit Breaker
Crank / charge the GFB-1 closing coil.
With the NFB-1 closed, attempt to close the GFB-1.
Confirm the electrical interlock prevented GFB-1 from closing.
Open the NFB-1 breaker.
Close the GFB-1 breaker.
Crank / charge the NFB-1 closing coil.
With the GFB-1 closed, attempt to close NFB-1.
Confirm the electrical interlock prevented the utility circuit breaker from closing.
Open the GFB-1 breaker.
At the upstream transformer, reinstate the RMU Outgoing breaker.
Confirm the MSB is supplied via the utility circuit breaker.
At the Generator Circuit Breaker, Remove LOTO.
Confirm no transfers occur and the MSB is remain energized by Utility supply.
Confirm no alarms are present on BMS network and local HMI.
C. Operation - Test Mode Generator Call To Start Validation - No Load
NOTE: Qualified personnel to operate equipment only - If operation of equipment can be conducted remotely, this is preferred to ensure all safety precautions are taken.
Notify down stream staff of numerous generator call to starts taking place over coming hours.
Confirm there are no alarms on the generator, ATS or UPS via the BMS network
On the ATS controller in auto mode followed by Engine Control Selection (ECS)
Confirm the generator receives a call to start
Confirm generator starts up, builds voltage and frequency.
Confirm generator voltage indication lamps illuminate.
Confirm ATS controller HMI depicts utility and generator source's available.
Confirm no ATS changeover
Cancel the engine test or no load test.
Confirm the generator call to start dissipates.
Confirm the local generator cooldown timer starts and at completion the generator stops.
Confirm ATS controller HMI depicts utility source available only.
D. Operation - Initial Condition / Normal Condition Verification
NOTE: Qualified personnel to operate equipment only - If operation of equipment can be conducted remotely, this is preferred to ensure all safety precautions are taken.
Confirm No Alarms on BMS
Confirm control power supply
Verify date and time sync correctly to local time
Source 1 set as utility source and preferred source
Source 2 set as Generator source
Utility Source is available and NFB-1 is closed
GFB-1 is open.
Generator Circuit Breaker is close.
Generator Controllers in AUTO
UPS in double-conversion mode. Maintenance bypass breakers are open.  No Open Transition Inhibit.
System Auto/Manual Selector Switch is in Auto.
Utility available Light ON
Generator AVAILABLE Light OFF
Load on Generator Light OFF
F. Operation - Auto Mode Transfer to Generator Operation  (S1 Preferred)- No Load

NOTE: Auto mode outage scenarios are to be performed a minimum of 1 time at transformer or generator level, all others can be performed via simulation of voltage sensing fuses to the phase failure relay.
NOTE: Qualified personnel to operate equipment only - If operation of equipment can be conducted remotely, this is preferred to ensure all safety precautions are taken.
Confirm there are no alarms on the generator, ATS or UPS via the BMS network
Simulate a utility source outage.
Confirm loss of utility source on the ATS controller.
Confirm the generator receives a call to start after S1 Outage Delay Timer elapse (3 seconds).
Confirm generator starts up immediately, builds voltage and frequency.
Confirm generator voltage indication lamps illuminate.
Confirm generator source stabilisation timer begins on ATS controller.
Generator source stabilisation timer elapses and utility circuit breaker opens after S1 Transient Delay timer (3s) elapses.
Confirm MSB supplied by generator.
Confirm completed changeover under 20 seconds
Confirm UPS Systems Register the return of mains supply and begin load hold off timer followed by load walk in
Confirm UPS Systems are now on rectifier supply
Confirm ATS controller HMI depicts generator source supplying the switchboard
Confirm there are no unanticipated alarms on generator, ATS or UPS via the BMS network

Confirm there are no alarms on the generator, ATS or UPS via the BMS network
Confirm utility source is available on the ATS controller.
Confirm utility stabilisation delay timer begins
Confirm ATS start counting for S2 Return Delay timer (540 second + staggering time 3mins for each generator)
Confirm generator circuit breaker opens with 3 seconds delay after S2 Transient Delay elapses.
Confirm the MSB is supplied via the utility.
Confirm UPS Systems Register the return of mains supply and begin load hold off timer followed by load walk in

Confirm ATS controller HMI depicts utility source supplying the power train unit.

Confirm there are no alarms on the generator, ATS or UPS via the BMS network

Confirm ATS controller HMI depicts utility source supplying the power train unit.

Verify MSB line up is supplied by utility source.

Confirm generator source stabilisation timer begins on ATS controller.

NOTE: Auto mode outage scenarios are to be performed a minimum of 1 time at transformer or generator level, all others can be performed via simulation of voltage sensing fuses to the phase failure relay.
NOTE: Qualified personnel to operate equipment only - If operation of equipment can be conducted remotely, this is preferred to ensure all safety precautions are taken.

Confirm the local generator cooldown timer starts and at completion the generator stops.
Reinstate the generator source by reinstate e-stop.

NOTE: Qualified personnel to operate equipment only - If operation of equipment can be conducted remotely, this is preferred to ensure all safety precautions are taken.
Remove the utility circuit breaker open command, preferred method is via relay.
Confirm the utility circuit breaker open command is removed.
Simulate a utility source outage.
Confirm loss of utility source on the ATS controller.
Confirm the generator receives a call to start after the source 1 outage delay timer elapses.

Confirm generator voltage indication lamps illuminate.

Confirm generator call to start remains latched.
Reinstate the generator circuit breaker close command.
Confirm the generator circuit breaker close command is reinstated.
Clear all active alarms on the ATS controller.
Generator circuit breaker closes.
Confirm the power train unit is supplied via the generator circuit breaker.
Confirm there are no unanticipated alarms on generator, ATS or UPS via the BMS network

NOTE: Qualified personnel to operate equipment only - If operation of equipment can be conducted remotely, this is preferred to ensure all safety precautions are taken.

Confirm the generator circuit breaker open command is removed.
Reinstate the utility source.

Bypass the utility stabilisation delay timer.
Confirm the generator circuit breaker attempts to open.
Confirm the ATS controller alarms "Fail to open generator circuit breaker".
Confirm the ATS controller alarm to the BMS network and local HMI.
Confirm no further action from ATS controller.
Confirm generator call to start remains latched.
Confirm the power train unit is supplied via the generator circuit breaker.

Confirm the utility circuit breaker close command is removed.
Reinstate the utility source.

Confirm utility stabilisation delay timer begins.

Confirm the utility circuit breaker attempts to close.
Confirm the ATS controller returns to available generator source.
Confirm the ATS controller alarms "Fail to close utility circuit breaker".
Confirm the ATS controller alarm to the BMS network and local HMI.
Confirm generator call to start remains latched.

NOTE: Qualified personnel to operate equipment only - If operation of equipment can be conducted remotely, this is preferred to ensure all safety precautions are taken.
Place generator in "Fail to Start" condition
Confirm generator Fail to Start alarm locally and on BMS.
Confirm ATS has no action and no alarm.
Confirm no alarm on BMS.
Confirm MSB is still on utility supply.

Confirm loss of utility source on the ATS controller.

Reinstate utility supply.

Confirm no alarm on ATS and BMS.

P. Operation - Loadbank Breaker Normal Operation
NOTE: Qualified personnel to operate equipment only - If operation of equipment can be conducted remotely, this is preferred to ensure all safety precautions are taken.
Place generator on loadbank by closing loadbank breaker.
Confirm MSB is supplied by utility source.
Confirm loadbank breaker is closed.

Confirm loadbank breaker fail to open.
Confirm loadbank breaker is not in fault or trip condition.
Confirm generator is still on loadbank.
Confirm generator breaker remains open and MSB is still operating on UPS supply.
Confirm ATS display "Fail to Open S3" and alarm recorded on BMS.
Reinstate all breaker position and loadbank breaker command.
Reinstate utility supply.

For outgoing circuits, Confirm the digital power meter voltage reference is connected to the output of each circuit breaker - DPM displays 0 volts with circuit breaker open.

For incoming circuits, isolate the upstream supply with the local breaker closed to confirm the digital power meter voltage reference is connected to the lineside of each circuit breaker - DPM displays 0 volts with upstream supply isolated.
Reinstate all circuit breakers to there nominal state.
Confirm no alarms are present on BMS network and local HMI.
Generate a surge arrestor fault alarm by removing one of the phase supply fuses.
Confirm surge arrestor fault alarm on BMS network and local HMI.
Reinstate the supply fuse.
Confirm surge arrestor fault alarm on BMS network and local HMI is no longer active.
Generate a loss of communications alarm by removing the BMS lan cable to the network switch.
Confirm Loss of Communications alarm on BMS network and local HMI.
Reinstate the network cable.
Confirm the alarm on BMS network and local HMI is no longer active.

Place the ATS controller into manual via the selector switch.

Confirm the electrical interlock prevented GFB-1 from closing.
Open the NFB-1 breaker.
Close the GFB-1 breaker.

Confirm the electrical interlock prevented the utility circuit breaker from closing.

lines.description: FUEL OIL SYSTEM
Description
While performing this procedure:

Items that do not apply shall be marked as N/A including a note as to why it does not apply.
Any discrepancies shall be entered as an issue with a detailed description.
Contractors and Vendors are responsible for safety of equipment and personnel while performing this procedure.  Concerns with any part of the procedure should be brought to the attention of the Commissioning Authority immediately.
Client approval is required to proceed if there are unresolved issues prior to the start of acceptance testing.
General Contractor

Attention: Contractor approval to perform this functional test procedure certifies that the equipment/systems covered by this document have been correctly installed, started up, and are ready for functional testing by the commissioning  authority.  Misrepresenting information on this document may result in rescheduling testing at additional cost to the responsible party.
Test Purpose

To confirm the proper operation of the equipment including programmable settings, optional features, and ancillary equipment. This script relates to Level 4 FPT of the Fuel Oil Transfer Pump , Underground Tank  and Day Tank at KUL21
1. Prerequisites
Confirm there are no critical issues open for equipment impacting Level 4.
Level 2 and Level 3 commissioning equipment start-up checklists are complete
Level 3 controls point-to-point and alarm verification checklists for equipment are completed.
Confirm all applicable equipment Method of Operating Procedure [MOPs] are created, approved, and reviewed for testing.
Equipment pre-test meeting is held with all parties to review the testing procedures, requirements and any constraints; all participants and affected personnel are notified prior to testing.
These functional test procedures reviewed and approved by the commissioning team.
Safeties and operating ranges reviewed and approved by Owner’s Representative.

All control system functions for this and all interlocking systems are programmed and operable per contract documents, including final set points and schedules with debugging, loop tuning and sensor calibrations completed.  All point to point verification has been completed, documented, reviewed and accepted.
BMS Controls: interlocks, graphics, automatic sequencing, and other controlling functions are complete.
2. Requested Staffing
The following staff members are available on-site to operate their equipment, assist and oversee completion of approved test procedure
Mechanical Contractor
Electrical Contractor
BMS Controls Vendor
Equipment Vendor
Owners Representative
3. Safety - Job Hazard Analysis [JHA]

The purpose of the JHA is to identify the Health / Safety Hazards and the Mitigation techniques to be used while performing this FPT.  All steps of this test script need to be reviewed to understand where each risk and mitigation apply.
Confirm JHA been carried out and recorded in iAuditor before commencing testing detailed in the test procedure
4. Safety Equipment
Digital Multi-meter to measure AC and DC voltage and current.
Electronic or infrared thermometer
Two-way Radios
Miscellaneous hand tools required for removing access panels and general access of equipment
Safety Equipment:  Hardhat, Safety glasses, and safety shoes required in construction areas.
5. Prerequisite  Documentation [Equipment Specific]
The following documents should be uploaded and available
Current Project Drawings [Mechanical, Electrical, and Plumbing]
Equipment Specific Approved Technical Submittal
Approved Sequence of Operation [SoO]
6. Equipment Identification
Manufacturer
Model Number
Serial Number
7. Initial Conditions

Record initial test conditions specific to unit being tested at component level.  Conditions recorded should be observed at unit locally and through BMS graphical interface.  Test section verifies components are operating and within range, as well as verifies components are represented correctly at the BMS level.

NOTE - All Dynamic Values will be visible in Screen Shot
RECORD SCREENSHOT of Control graphic and attach to this test script line item for reference to all pre test initial conditions
Review Screenshot data and confirm value inputs are reliable and easily readable at BMS front end.
Unit Identification and description is correct on the graphic display
Unit is in the correct location on floor plan layout
All graphic animations of equipment actions have been programmed and are complete
All BMS points are correctly and neatly represented on the graphic display
Review & Verify the Graphics are correct and represent all devices fitted in the field
Review & Verify the Graphics are as per Status A Approved Graphics
Verify & record the firmware version
8. Pre-Record Initial setpoints per SOO, Specification, or Equipment Submittal to confirm system has been configured to control to the correct parameters.
Note - SOO requirements supercede conflicting parameters.
RECORD & CONFIRM THE FOLLOWING
DT Fuel Level [High-High] = 95% (950L)
DT Fuel Level [High] = 90% (900L)
DT Fuel Level [Low] = 50% (500L)
DT Fuel Level [Low-Low] = 25% (250L)
FUT Fuel Level [High-High] = 90% (90,000L)
FUT Fuel Level [High] = 80% (80,000L)
FUT Fuel Level [Low] = 50% (50,000L)
FUT Fuel Level [Low-Low] = 20% (20,000L)
9. Equipment Physical Inspection and Preliminary Checks
Inspect equipment installation for compliance with approved submittal, construction details, and industry standards.
Confirm installation is inspected for compliance with approved submittal, construction details, and industry standards.
Confirm a complete L2/3 verification of this item of equipment has been conducted prior to L4 test commencing
Conduct a pre physical inspection of equipment prior to L4 test commencing
10. Functional Performance Test - Fuel Oil System (FOS)
FOS Normal Operation - Call For Fuel Day Tank
With the transfer pump in operation, simulate the DT fuel level < 50 % (500L) (Low Level)
Confirm DT [Low Level] alarm is generated in BMS
Confirm [Call For Fuel] Alarm is activate in BMS
Confirm duty transfer pump is START running
Confirm associate fuel supply pipe (suction valve) motorize valve OPEN
Confirm associate fuel return pipe motorize valve OPEN
Confirm the Daytank inlet valve OPEN
Confirm the Return by-pass pipe supply valve CLOSE
Continue to simulate the DT fuel level at 25% (250L) (Low-Low level)
Confirm DT [Low-Low Level] alarm is generated in BMS
Confirm alarm is generated in Fuel System PLC control HMI
Confirm alarm is generated in Generator controller
Continue to simulate the DT fuel level <10% (100L) (Low-Low level) for 5sec (adj.)
Confirm associate GEN is STOP
Confirm duty transfer pump is STOP
Confirm the DT inlet valve CLOSE
Confirm alarm horn & light is activated at the DT control panel
FOS Emergency Operation - Call For Stop
Simulate the DT fuel level at 95% (950L) (High-High Level)

Confirm alarm is generated in Fuel System PLC control HMI
Confirm [Call For Stop] Alarm is activate in BMS
Continue to simulate the DT fuel level at 90% (900L) (High Level)
Confirm DT [High Level] alarm is generated in BMS
Confirm alarm is generated in Fuel System PLC control HMI
Confirm [Call For Stop] Alarm is activate in BMS
Continue to simulate the DT fuel level >90% (900L) (High Level) for 10sec (adj.)
Confirm duty transfer pump is STOP
Confirm the Daytank inlet valve CLOSE
Confirm the Supply (suction valve) motorize valve is CLOSE
Confirm the Return motorize valve is OPEN
Confirm the Return by-pass pipe supply motorize valve is OPEN

Confirm duty transfer pump continue operate

Confirm duty transfer pump failed to start

Confirm standby transfer pump take over operation
Continue fail standby transfer pump
Confirm that entire fuel transfer operation stop
Confirm all motorize valve is closing
Reinstate back to normal

Confirm UG1 tank motorised valve supply and return [CLOSED]

Confirm FOT [High Level] alarm is generated in BMS
Continue refilling to simulate fuel level at 90% High Level alarm for 5sec (adj.)
